newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DUVAL KEEPS DORAL-RYDER LEAD AFTER ROLLERCOASTER ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DUVAL KEEPS DORAL-RYDER LEAD AFTER ROLLERCOASTER ROUND.

text.p: David Duval rode a rollercoaster round to a one-stroke lead after three rounds of the Doral-Ryder Open golf tournament on Saturday.
Duval carded nine birdies, four bogeys, one double bogey and just three pars on Doral's Blue Monster course for a two-under-par 70 and a 12-under 204 total after 54 holes.
"This round was sure something," said Duval, who had just one par among the last 11 holes.
Duval's crazy round saw him as much as two strokes in the lead and as far back as three strokes behind.

Nick Price of Zimbabwe was one stroke back at 11-under after a fairly uneven, though comparatively uneventful, round of 70 himself. And Australian Steve Elkington was alone in third at 10-under, after also posting 70.
Greg Norman, the overnight co-leader with Duval and a three-time former champion at Doral, lost four strokes on the last six holes, double-bogeying 18 to drop to eight-under and a tie for sixth.
Duval missed an eagle putt of six feet on the 10th hole, and birdied the 11th to take a share of the lead with Price, who shot a blistering 31 on the front nine.
Duval then put together a string of three successive bogeys on holes 13 through 15, but birdied the next two to regain the lead.
He made his last bogey with a drive up against a ficus tree on the 18th hole -- Doral's toughest -- the original Blue Monster which gave its nickname to the entire course.
With 18 holes to go, Price put himself in good position to win his third consecutive tournament after breaking a 15-month drought with back-to-back wins in South Africa.
Price posted five birdies and no bogeys on the front nine. He followed with three bogeys and no birdies coming in.
"The way the course is set up, it lends itself to this kind of play," Price said.
"You can be aggressive and be rewarded, but then it can just grab you."
